    UNDP Funding Compendium 2025

    Regular Resources

    Lion’s share goes to programmes


    The lion’s share of the core programme budget for 2022–2025 is channelled through country programmes.

    Source: [Add source]

    Strong support for least developed and low-income countries

    Over 80 percent of core resources are allocated to least developed countries where development needs are greatest, and over 70 percent to low-income countries.



    2022–2025 distribution of regular (core) resources by development status, Core: TRAC-1, TRAC-2 and TRAC-3

    Source: DP/2025/23 Annex 1

    2022–2025 distribution of regular (core) resources by country typology, Core: TRAC-1, TRAC-2 and TRAC-3

    Source: DP/2025/23 Annex 1

    Africa receives the largest share

    In line with development needs, the largest share of core resources is allocated to Africa, followed by Asia and the Arab States.


    2022–2025 distribution of regular (core) resources by region
    Core: TRAC-1, TRAC-2 and TRAC-3

    Source: DP/2025/23 Annex 1

    The institutional budget enables programmatic impact

    UNDP’s institutional budget supports investments in institutional capacity, development effectiveness, the maintenance of the highest levels of independent oversight, transparency and accountability, and special-purpose initiatives (UNV and UNCDF).


    Source: DP/2025/23 Table 1

    Top core contributors

    In 2025, UNDP received $442 million in core contributions, of which 37 percent were backed by multi-year commitments, down from 40 percent in 2024.


    *Includes core contributions for 2024 received in 2025
    **Includes core contributions for 2026 received in 2025

    12 partners with multi-year pledges to regular resources

    In 2025, UNDP received $442 million in core contributions, of which 37 percent were backed by multi-year commitments, down from 40 percent in 2024.


    Contributors to regular resources, 2025

    Source: DP/2025/23 Table 1

    Government contributions to local office costs

    Annual government contributions to local office costs (GLOC) are an important source of revenue and take the form of cash or in-kind contributions from host governments. In low- and middle-income countries, $39 million was received in 2025 ($29 million in 2024), consisting of $31 million in cash contributions and $8 million of in-kind contributions for premises and utilities.
